title: Apply to 100 jobs in one night with ChatGPT
summary: ChatGPT's agent mode finds jobs on LinkedIn and Indeed, tailors your resume for each role, and applies for you while you watch the browser work.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A paid ChatGPT plan (Plus or higher). Agent mode isn't on the free plan.
- A LinkedIn account and an Indeed account, both logged in.
- Your current resume as a file (PDF or Word).
- 2 to 4 hours, since you stay nearby to clear CAPTCHAs.

steps.title: Load your resume and map roles
steps.text:
This maps your resume to the job titles and keywords worth targeting.

1. Open a **new chat** in ChatGPT.
2. Upload your resume as an attachment.
3. Paste the prompt below and press Enter.

``` Prompt 1: Recruiter map
Act as a senior recruiter. Based on my resume, list the 20 job titles I'm most qualified for and the exact keywords ATS systems scan for in each one.
```

> If most jobs later come back with a match score of 0, your titles were too broad. Re-run this prompt and ask it to be more specific.

steps.title: Build your master resume
steps.text:
Stay in the same chat. Paste this:

``` Prompt 2: Master resume
Turn my resume into a master version I can tweak for any role in seconds. Run it through the Google XYZ formula (Accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z) and kill everything a hiring manager would reject in one glance.
```

The XYZ formula forces every bullet into one shape: accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z. So "Managed social media" becomes "Grew Instagram from 12K to 180K followers in 9 months by shipping a daily short-form video pipeline." Recruiters skim in about seven seconds, and bullets like this survive the skim.

"Kill everything a hiring manager would reject" strips out:

- Vague verbs: responsible for, involved in, helped with, worked on.
- Buzzwords: synergy, ninja, rockstar, thought leader.
- Unquantified claims: "increased sales significantly" becomes "increased sales 34% QoQ".
- Blocks of prose. Bullets only, one or two lines each.

Save the result as your master resume. Every application in Step 4 is tweaked from this one file.

steps.title: Turn on agent mode
steps.text:
Still in the same chat.

1. Click the **+** button under the message box.
2. Turn on **Agent Mode**. Some accounts call it **ChatGPT agent**.
3. If it asks, allow the agent to open a browser for you.
4. Log into LinkedIn and Indeed in your normal browser first.

> If you connect the Indeed app inside ChatGPT (Apps sidebar, then Indeed, then **Connect**), the agent can pull listings without leaving the chat. It dodges a lot of the CAPTCHA trouble.

steps.title: Search and apply to jobs
steps.text:
Paste this:

``` Prompt 3: Search and score
Go to LinkedIn and Indeed. Find every job matching my target titles from Step 1, posted in the last 7 days. Build me a spreadsheet with: job link, company, location, match score (0-100), and a custom-tailored resume version for each one. Prioritize "Easy Apply" (LinkedIn) and "Apply now" (Indeed) listings - flag anything that redirects to Workday, Greenhouse, or Lever as a separate manual list.
```

The agent opens a browser window you can watch. It runs the searches, filters by date, scores each job against your resume, and builds the sheet. This takes 10 to 30 minutes.

**Easy Apply** is where the automation actually works: one click, resume pre-filled. Postings that redirect to Workday, Greenhouse or Lever need account creation and custom answers, so batch those for a manual session later.

Once the sheet is ready, paste this:

``` Prompt 4: Auto-apply
Go through the top 100 matches from the spreadsheet and apply to each one. For every application: use the tailored resume version, customize any short-answer fields based on the job description, and log the submission status in the sheet. If a listing asks for a cover letter, write one under 250 words that sounds like a real person - no "I am writing to express my interest" openers.
```

The agent starts applying, clicking into each posting in the browser. A realistic run is 50 to 150 applications over 2 to 4 hours before it hits a rate limit or a wall of custom questions and stops.

>! The agent applies to real jobs with your real accounts. Watch the browser window, and clear CAPTCHAs and custom questions when it pauses.

> Tell the agent to skip any job with more than three short-answer questions and log it to a manual list, so a few long forms don't stall the whole run.

> Some companies block automated applications and reject them silently. Apply to those by hand.

steps.title: Make the interviews more likely
steps.text:
Two things decide whether you wake up to interviews or silence.

> Tailoring beats volume. The same resume sent 100 times gets one or two interviews. The per-role resume from Step 2 sent 100 times gets eight to fifteen. The tailoring does the work, not the automation.

> Time the run so applications land early in the recruiter's morning in the target market, not at 3 AM. Applications read at the top of the day get seen; the rest get buried.

title: Test your launch on an AI crowd with MiroFish
summary: MiroFish builds a crowd of AI people, shows them your launch, and reports how the market might react, so you can fix the price or message before you go live.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A Mac or Windows computer.
- Node.js 18 or higher.
- Python 3.11 or 3.12.
- uv, the Python package manager.
- An LLM API key. The repo recommends Alibaba's Qwen-plus through DashScope, but any OpenAI-compatible API works.
- A Zep Cloud key for the agents' memory. The free monthly tier is enough to start.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.text:
``` Command: Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/666ghj/MiroFish.git
cd MiroFish
```

steps.title: Get your two API keys
steps.text:
- LLM key: sign up at a provider and copy an API key, its base URL, and the model name. The repo's default is Alibaba's Bailian / DashScope platform (qwen-plus), but any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, such as OpenAI or Gemini through a compatible proxy.
- Zep Cloud key: create a free account at getzep.com and grab the API key. The free monthly quota covers light use.

steps.title: Set up your environment file
steps.text:
Copy the example file.

``` Command: Copy the env file
cp .env.example .env
```

Open .env and fill in your keys.

``` Command: Your .env values
LLM_API_KEY=your_api_key
LLM_BASE_URL=https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 LLM_MODEL_NAME=qwen-plusZEP_API_KEY=your_zep_api_key
```

> Swap LLM_BASE_URL and LLM_MODEL_NAME for whatever provider you are using.

steps.title: Install everything
steps.text:
One command installs the lot (root, frontend, and backend).

``` Command: Install everything
npm run setup:all
```

Prefer to do it in stages?

``` Command: Install in stages
npm run setup
npm run setup:backend
```

steps.title: Start MiroFish
steps.text:
``` Command: Start MiroFish
npm run dev
```

Then open these in your browser:

- Frontend (the dashboard): http://localhost:3000
- Backend API: http://localhost:5001

> Want them separately? Run npm run backend and npm run frontend. Docker alternative: after Step 3, run docker compose up -d for the same ports.

> Want it fully local and free, with no cloud API bill? There is a community fork, github.com/nikmcfly/MiroFish-Offline, that swaps in a local stack (Neo4j and Ollama). The trade-off: you need a capable machine, and local models are weaker than frontier ones.

steps.title: Run your first simulation
steps.text:
This is the part the video is really selling. In the dashboard:

1. Upload your seed material: whatever you are about to put out, such as your launch post, landing-page copy, the new price, the ad creative, or a short product description. It also accepts research docs or background text.
2. Describe what you want to know, in plain language. For example: "I'm launching this $49/mo SaaS to indie founders. Test how they react to the price and the main headline. I'm worried it reads as too expensive and too generic."
3. Keep the first run small: a modest number of agents and under about 40 rounds. This controls cost while you learn how it behaves.
4. Run it. MiroFish builds a knowledge graph from your material, generates a crowd of AI personas with different backgrounds, lets them react and talk to each other, and tracks how opinions shift over time. Tip: Use a cheaper, faster model for early experiments and save the expensive model for final runs. Watch your LLM provider's usage dashboard for the first few runs so there are no bill surprises.

steps.title: Read the report and dig in
steps.text:
When the run finishes you get two things:

- A prediction report: how the market responded, with sentiment, the main objections, what landed, and what fell flat.
- A living world you can explore: chat directly with any AI agent (for example, "why did you bounce off the price?") and ask the Report Agent follow-up questions.

Use the objections and framing problems it surfaces to fix your real launch, then re-run to compare if you want.

steps.title: Know the limits before you trust it
steps.text:
MiroFish gives you directional signal, not a verdict. Keep these in mind:

- Simulated is not real. Treat the results as hypotheses to test, not facts.
- Garbage in, garbage out. The personas are only as good as your seed material and your prompt.
- Costs scale with realism. A run with thousands of customers is possible but expensive. Most of the value comes from smaller, well-framed runs.

>! MiroFish is AGPL-3.0 licensed. That is fine for personal or internal use, but read the license before you build a commercial product on top of it.

title: Set up a free AI sales agent with Harvey
summary: Harvey is a free, open-source AI agent that finds leads, writes personal cold emails, sends them and chases replies, all on the Claude plan you already pay for.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A Mac or Windows computer.
- A paid Claude plan (Pro or Max). Max is best if you want Harvey running all day.
- A paid Instantly plan to send the emails. Their Growth plan or higher includes the API access Harvey needs.
- About 10 minutes.

steps.title: Install Claude Code
steps.text:
This is the only thing you set up by hand. Everything after this, Claude does for you.

On Mac:

1. Open the Terminal app. Press Cmd + Space, type Terminal, and press Enter.
2. Paste the line below and press Enter.

``` Command (Mac): Install Claude Code
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

On Windows:

1. Open PowerShell. Press Start, type PowerShell, and press Enter.
2. Paste the line below and press Enter.

``` Command (Windows): Install Claude Code
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then on both:

1. Close the terminal window and open a new one.
2. Type the command below and press Enter.
3. A browser window opens. Sign in with the same account as your paid Claude plan.

``` Command: Start Claude Code
claude
```

> If Claude later asks to install Git or Python, say yes. It needs them to set Harvey up, and it can install them for you.

steps.title: Let Claude install Harvey
steps.text:
Now you hand the rest to Claude. In the same claude session, paste this one message and press Enter.

``` Prompt: Set up Harvey
Set up Harvey for me from scratch. Clone
https://github.com/ethanplusai/harvey.git into a new folder, install everything it needs (including anything missing on my computer like Python or Git), then run Harvey's setup wizard end to end. Train Harvey on my product from my website, connect my email tool, and get it running. Ask me for anything you need along the way, and explain each step in simple words.
```

Then just follow along. Claude installs the parts, asks you a few questions, and sets everything up. That is the whole point of running this through Claude.

> Harvey is not a Claude plugin, so there is no /skills step here. It is its own app that uses Claude as its brain. You confirm it is set up by opening the dashboard in Step 4.

steps.title: Tell Harvey what you sell
steps.text:
During setup, Harvey asks a few simple things. This is the part that makes it work.

- Your product: paste your website link. Harvey reads your site and learns your product and your ideal customer on its own. No website? Just type the answers to its questions.
- Your ideal customer: the kind of business you want (industry, size, location).
- Your email tool: your Instantly API key, so Harvey can send. Find it in Instantly under Settings -> Integrations -> API Keys.

>! Skip the LinkedIn option. Using it can get your LinkedIn account restricted. Harvey finds leads from web search and company websites instead.

> Say you build websites. You tell Harvey that, and it finds local businesses that match, researches each one, and writes a real, tailored cold email per business, not a template.

> If Instantly gives a 401 error, your API key is wrong or your plan does not include API access. Make a new key in Instantly under Settings -> Integrations -> API Keys.

steps.title: Start it and watch your pipeline
steps.text:
Once setup is done, just tell Claude start Harvey. Or run the command below yourself.

``` Command: Start Harvey
harvey run
```

Harvey now works on its own in the background. It will:

- Find new leads that match your ideal customer.
- Research each one.
- Write a personalized cold email for each.
- Send them through Instantly.
- Read the replies and respond to move toward a meeting.
- Keep repeating, on a schedule you set.

To see everything in one place, open this in your browser.

``` Open in browser: Live dashboard
http://localhost:5555
```

That is your live dashboard: every lead, every campaign, every reply. To stop Harvey at any time, go back to the terminal and press Ctrl + C. Nothing sends while it is stopped.

> Harvey runs while your computer is on and the terminal is open. For true around-the-clock running you can later move it to a server, but that is advanced and you do not need it to start.

> If it says command not found: harvey, tell Claude "the harvey command isn't found, fix it" and it will sort out the setup for you.

> If Harvey isn't finding leads, free web search gets rate-limited. Serper, the search service, gives 2,500 free searches to start; after that its cheapest paid plan is $50 for 50,000 searches. Ask Claude to add a Serper API key for reliable results.

steps.title: Protect your email before sending
steps.text:
Cold email done wrong will get your email address blocked. Two minutes of care here saves weeks of pain.

- Use a separate sending domain, not your main company email. Example: getyourbrand.com instead of yourbrand.com.
- Turn on Instantly's warmup and leave it on for 2 to 4 weeks before sending real volume.
- Start small: 10 to 20 emails a day, then raise it slowly.
- Always honor opt-outs. If someone says stop or unsubscribe, Harvey already treats that as final. Keep it that way.

>! This is not legal advice. If you send at large scale or into regulated industries, talk to a lawyer first.

> Emails going to spam is almost always a domain problem, not your writing. Check that your sending domain is set up and warmed up, and cut your daily volume in half.

title: Build a hospital booking site that calls patients
summary: Build a hospital appointment website where every booking triggers an AI voice agent to call and confirm, then saves the recording and details to one dashboard.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A Mac or Windows computer with Claude Code installed.
- An OmniDimension account for the AI voice agent, plus a phone number (buy one inside OmniDimension).
- A Vercel account to put the site live.
- A Supabase account to store bookings and call data.
- A Resend account (or any email tool) to email you the recording and details.
- About 30 to 45 minutes for a first version.

>! Steps 1, 2 and 4 are mostly simple. The real work is Step 3, where the booking has to trigger the call and the call has to report back. That is what makes it a real system and not just a nice-looking website. Slow down there.

steps.title: Build the website
steps.text:
Open Claude Code in an empty folder. Paste this:

``` Prompt: Build the site
Build a hospital appointment booking website in Next.js and Tailwind.

Pages: Home, Doctors, Book Appointment, Contact.
The booking form collects: patient name, phone number, doctor, date, time, and reason for visit. Design: clean, calm, medical. White with soft blue. Modern and mobile-first. Keep everything in one project I can deploy to Vercel.
```

Let it build, open the preview, and keep asking for changes until it looks right:

``` Prompt: Refine the look
Make the hero simpler. Bigger heading. Move the booking button to the top. Round the form corners.
```

Then give it your real content so it stops looking like a demo:

``` Prompt: Add your real content
Replace the placeholder content with my real hospital.
Doctors: [name and specialty for each]
Services: [list]
Timings: [list]
Contact: [phone, email, address]
Use the logo and photos I am adding to the project folder.
```

> Drop your logo and photos into the project folder first, then tell Claude the file names. It will place them for you.

steps.title: Build the AI voice agent
steps.text:
Go to OmniDimension and create a new Voice AI assistant. Pick a warm, natural voice, then give it these instructions (paste and edit the name):

``` Prompt: Voice agent instructions
You are the front desk receptionist for [Hospital Name].
You are calling a patient to confirm the appointment they just booked. Be warm, clear and quick.

Do this:
1. Greet them by name.
2. Confirm the doctor, the date and the time.
3. Ask if that time still works for them.
4. If yes, confirm it and thank them.
5. If no, tell them you will note a reschedule request and someone will call back.

Keep the call under a minute. Never give medical advice.
```

Then:

- Buy a phone number inside OmniDimension (or import your Twilio number) and attach it to this agent. This is the number that will call patients.
- Copy your API key and your Agent ID. You need both in Step 3.

> Place a test call to your own number before wiring anything. Fix the voice and the script here, not later.

steps.title: Connect everything and go live
steps.text:
This is where the site starts working like a real system. Go slowly here.

First, wire the booking. Back in Claude Code, paste this and fill in your IDs:

``` Prompt: Wire the booking
When someone submits the booking form, do three things on the server:
1. Save the booking to Supabase.
2. Call the OmniDimension API to start a confirmation call to the patient's phone number, using Agent ID [your agent id].
3. Email me the booking details.
Read these from environment variables, do not hardcode them:
OMNIDIM_API_KEY, OMNIDIM_AGENT_ID, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY, MY_EMAIL. Show me the .env file I need to fill in.
```

Next, deploy. Add the Vercel plugin in Claude Code, then ask it to deploy:

``` Prompt: Deploy to Vercel
Add Vercel. Deploy this project to my Vercel account and give me the live link.
```

Then set your environment variables in Vercel (Project -> Settings -> Environment Variables) using your .env values, and redeploy.

Last, close the loop from the call back to you. In OmniDimension, add a webhook that fires after each call and point it at your live site (for example https://yoursite.com/api/call-result). Then in Claude Code:

``` Prompt: Receive the call result
Add an API route at /api/call-result that receives OmniDimension's webhook after a call. Save the recording link, transcript and outcome to Supabase against the matching booking. Email me the recording link and the patient details.
```

Now the full loop runs on its own: patient books, the AI calls in about a minute, and the result and recording come back to Supabase and your inbox.

steps.title: Connect Supabase and get your dashboard
steps.text:
Create a free project on Supabase. In the SQL editor, create two tables:

``` SQL: Create the tables
create table bookings (
id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
name text,
phone text,
doctor text,
appointment_date date,
appointment_time text,
reason text,
status text default 'pending',
created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table call_logs (
id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
booking_id uuid references bookings(id),
recording_url text,
transcript text,
outcome text,
created_at timestamptz default now()
);
```

Copy your Project URL and anon key from Settings -> API and put them in your env (same names as Step 3). Then add a simple admin view. In Claude Code:

``` Prompt: Build the admin page
Add a password-protected admin page at /admin.
Show a table of all bookings with their status, plus the linked call recording and outcome for each. Let me update a booking's status from this page.
```

Now everything lives in one place: bookings, call recordings and status, all editable by you.

steps.title: Test before you go live
steps.text:
Book a fake appointment with your own number and check the whole loop: the call, the email, and the dashboard all work.

>! Calls cost money. You pay for the phone number and for each minute of calling. Start small and watch your usage.

>! Only call people who gave their number to book. Confirming their own appointment is fine. Do not use this to cold-call strangers.

title: Turn Claude into your Instagram manager with Ootto
summary: Connect Claude to Instagram through Ootto, paste one prompt, and Claude studies your profile and builds a full week of Reels with hooks, scripts, captions and direction.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Custom connectors aren't on the free plan.
- Your Instagram login, to connect your account through Ootto.
- 5 minutes.

>! Claude writes everything for your Reels and drafts it into Ootto, but the animated graphics, the voiceover audio and the music come out as direction (what to make and the vibe), not finished files. You still render those in your own tools. Whether Ootto posts for you automatically depends on your Ootto account's publishing setting.

steps.title: Connect Ootto to Claude
steps.text:
1. In Claude, go to Customize -> Connectors.
2. Click Add Custom Connector.
3. Name it Ootto, paste the URL below into the URL field, and leave advanced settings empty.

``` Connector URL
https://mcp.ootto.ai/mcp
```

4. Click **Add**, then **Connect**, then **Allow** when Claude asks for permission.
5. A login screen opens. Log into Ootto, pick **Instagram**, and click **Allow access**.

You'll see Ootto listed under your connectors with an active status.

> No **Add Custom Connector** button? You're likely on the free plan. Custom connectors need Pro or higher.

> If Ootto won't connect, re-check the URL is exactly https://mcp.ootto.ai/mcp with advanced settings empty. If the Instagram link fails, log out of Ootto, log back in, and link Instagram again from scratch.

steps.title: Paste the master prompt
steps.text:
Open a normal Claude chat and paste this whole block.

``` Prompt: Instagram growth manager
You are my Instagram growth manager. You have access to my Instagram account through the Ootto connector. Work through this in order, and ask me to approve before anything gets published.

STEP 1 - Study my account
Use the Ootto tools to pull my profile and my last 30 to 60 posts. Look at:
- Which Reels and posts got the most views, likes, saves and shares
- The hooks and opening lines that performed best
- My average Reel length, my posting times and days
- The hashtags and topics that show up in my best posts
Then tell me, in plain language, what my niche is, who my audience is, and my top 3 content pillars (the themes that actually perform).

STEP 2 - Find what is working right now
Search the web for 8 to 10 trending topics, formats and angles in my niche this week. Keep only the ones that fit my pillars and my audience.

STEP 3 - Build a 7-day Reel plan
Give me one Reel per day for the next 7 days. For each day, write:
- Day and best time to post (based on my own data)
- Title hook: the short text that sits on the first frame
- Spoken hook: the first line I say
- Full script: word for word, in my voice, matched to how my best Reels sound
- Caption: ready to paste
- Hashtags: 5 to 10, based on what works for me
- Visual direction: what is on screen, scene by scene
- Voiceover direction: tone and pace
- Music direction: the kind of track and the vibe
Keep the writing simple and human. Match my tone, not a generic influencer tone.

STEP 4 - Draft them into Ootto
Using the Ootto tools, save each Reel's caption and plan into my account as a draft or scheduled post. If Ootto can schedule them to post automatically, set them up but do not publish anything until I say go. If Ootto cannot schedule, just give me everything above so I can post it myself.

Start with Step 1 now. After each step, pause and show me the result before moving on.
```

steps.title: Approve each stage
steps.text:
Claude works through it one step at a time and stops for you to check each stage:

- After Step 1: a plain-English read on your niche, audience, and top 3 content pillars.
- After Step 2: a shortlist of trending angles that fit your page.
- After Step 3: 7 full Reels with hook, script, caption, hashtags, posting time, plus visual, voiceover and music direction.
- After Step 4: everything drafted into Ootto, ready for you to approve.

Nothing posts until you say go. Read each Reel, tweak anything that doesn't sound like you, then approve.

> If it skips straight to writing without studying your account, tell it: "Do Step 1 first, pull my real posts through Ootto before writing anything."

> If the output sounds generic, tell it: "Rewrite in my voice, match the tone of my 3 best-performing Reels."

> If Claude says it can't see your posts, make sure Ootto shows connected in your connector list, then start a fresh chat.

steps.title: Run it again every week
steps.text:
Once you like the output, run it again any time by pasting the same prompt. Claude re-studies your latest posts and builds a fresh week.

> If your Ootto account has scheduling turned on, ask Claude to schedule the approved Reels across the week so they post on their own.

title: Let 7 AI advisors debate your business decision
summary: Roast Room is a free Claude skill that seats 7 AI advisors, each built from a real founder's work, to argue your decision, score the options, and hand you a PDF verdict.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A laptop (Mac or Windows).
- A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Claude Code and the advisor sub-agents run on your plan, no API key needed.
- Node.js 20 or newer (free, link in Tools).
- 5 minutes.

steps.title: Install Claude Code
steps.text:
On Mac, open Terminal and paste:

``` Command (Mac): Install Claude Code
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

On Windows, open PowerShell and paste:

``` Command (Windows): Install Claude Code
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

Once it finishes, type claude and press Enter. Log in with your Claude account when it asks.

> If the claude command is not found, close and reopen the terminal, then try again.

steps.title: Install Node.js
steps.text:
Roast Room runs a small local app that shows the 7 advisors around a table. That needs Node. Go to nodejs.org (in Tools), download version 20 or newer, and install it with all the default settings.

To check it worked, open your terminal and type:

``` Command: Check Node
node --version
```

If you see a number like v20.something, you're good.

> If the node command is not found, reinstall Node from nodejs.org and reopen your terminal.

steps.title: Install the Roast Room skill
steps.text:
Open Claude Code and paste this one message:

``` Prompt: Install Roast Room
Clone github.com/nateherkai/roast-room and set it up for me.

Run git clone, cd into the folder, confirm the
.claude/skills/roast-room folder is in place, then run /skills so I can see all 7 advisor sub-agents loaded.
```

Claude handles the clone and setup itself.

> If the advisors don't show in /skills, paste in Claude Code: "Reload the skills directory and run /skills again."

steps.title: Start the room
steps.text:
Still in your terminal, inside the roast-room folder, run:

``` Command: Start the room
npm start
```

Then open http://localhost:4730 in your browser. Leave this tab open. This is the live room where you'll watch the advisors debate.

> If npm start throws an error, make sure you're inside the roast-room folder first (cd roast-room). If the room page won't load, make sure the npm start terminal is still running, then refresh the page.

steps.title: Run your first roast
steps.text:
Open Claude Code in the same folder (type claude), then paste your decision:

``` Command: Run a roast
/roast-room [your decision here]
```

A good prompt gives the council what it needs. Example:

``` Prompt: Example decision
/roast-room I run a D2C skincare brand doing $40k a month with 1 full-time hire. Should I raise prices by 30%, launch a cheaper line, or spend the next 90 days only on content and keep prices flat? I have $25k in the bank. Success is $70k a month by March. I'm leaning toward the cheaper line because volume feels safer.
```

Include: the decision, 2 to 3 options, your numbers (revenue, cash, team), your limits (deadline, budget), what success looks like, and which way you're leaning. The Chair asks follow-up questions if anything is missing.

>! A full 7-advisor council uses real plan credit (21 sub-agent runs). For smaller calls, use /roast-room --quick [decision] (4 advisors, 2 rounds), /roast-room --seats hormozi,buffett [decision] (only the advisors you pick), or /roast-room ask hormozi [question] (one answer from one seat).

steps.title: Watch the council and get your verdict
steps.text:
Each of the 7 advisors argues from their own pillar:

- Jeff Bezos: strategy and reversibility, is this the right bet?
- Paul Graham: product-market fit, do people actually want it?
- Alex Hormozi: offer, pricing, sales, will people pay?
- Gary Vaynerchuk: attention and marketing, where do eyeballs come from?
- Dan Martell: people, hiring, your calendar, who does this work?

title: Build a music streaming site with Claude Code
summary: Describe a Spotify-style music site to Claude Code and it builds the search, audio player and track art, then helps you fix bugs and get it online.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- Claude Code installed and working.
- A folder of songs you own or are allowed to use (mp3 or similar).
- A few background images for the tracks.
- A rough idea of the look you want (colours, vibe, layout).

>! Use music and images you actually have rights to. If this goes public, other people's songs and copyrighted art can get the site taken down.

steps.title: Describe the site in one prompt
steps.text:
Give Claude one clear, detailed prompt and let it build the full site, structure, design, search and audio player included. The more detail you give, the less back-and-forth later.

A strong prompt covers:

- What the site is, such as "a music streaming site like Spotify, but smaller".
- The main sections: home, search, and a now-playing bar.
- The player behaviour: play, pause, skip, progress bar, duration.
- The look: dark theme, colours, font feel.
- Anything unique, such as songs grouped by place or mood.

Claude builds the structure, design, interactions, search and audio player in one go.

> Describe behaviour, not code. "The player should keep playing while I browse other pages" is better than trying to name a technical approach.

steps.title: Add your songs and images
steps.text:
Drop your songs and images into the project, then ask Claude to organise them. It handles the boring part for you:

- Renames every file into a clean, consistent format.
- Matches each track to its background image.
- Pulls the real duration off each track so the player shows correct times.

> You don't hand-label anything. Give it the raw files and one instruction: "organise these and wire them into the player."

steps.title: Show Claude the bug, don't explain it
steps.text:
When something breaks, stop trying to describe it in words. Record your screen while using the broken site, then upload the recording to Claude.

Why this works better than typing:

- Claude sees the actual behaviour: a broken layout, a missing image, a player that won't play.
- No guessing on your side about what to call the problem.
- It spots the cause and fixes it directly.

> In the recording, do the exact thing that breaks, click the button, load the page, hit play, so the failure is on screen.

steps.title: Finalise and publish
steps.text:
Ask Claude to finalise the project. It will:

- Optimise the assets (images and audio) so the site loads faster.
- Clean up leftover and unused project files.
- Prepare everything for hosting.

Then ask Claude for a step-by-step guide to put the site online. It gives you the exact steps to publish: which files to upload, where, and in what order.

> The real upgrade here isn't the website. It's treating Claude like a developer who can build, test, debug and ship, start to finish.

title: Set up JARVIS, your open-source voice assistant
summary: Install Claude Code, hand it an open-source assistant repo, add an ElevenLabs voice and your own tools, and get a voice assistant that reads your morning out loud.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A computer running macOS 13+, Windows 10 (1809+), or Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ / Debian 10+).
- 4 GB or more of RAM and an internet connection.
- A paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise). Claude Code is not on the free Claude.ai plan.
- A GitHub account.
- An ElevenLabs account. The free tier gives about 10,000 voice credits a month to start.
- The GitHub link for the assistant project you want to install.

>! Replace YOUR-REPO-URL everywhere below with the actual repo link from the video. The steps stay the same whichever open-source assistant project you use.

steps.title: Install Claude Code
steps.text:
Claude Code is the agent that installs and runs everything. Open your terminal and run the command for your system.

``` Command (macOS / Linux / WSL): Install Claude Code
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

``` Command (Windows PowerShell): Install Claude Code
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

``` Command (any OS, needs Node.js 18+): Install Claude Code
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

Then confirm it installed:

``` Command: Check the install
claude --version
claude doctor
```

The first time you launch it, it opens your browser to sign in with your Claude account.

``` Command: Start Claude Code
claude
```

> If you get command not found: claude, close and reopen your terminal (the installer updates your PATH). Still stuck? Run claude doctor and it tells you exactly what's wrong.

steps.title: Hand Claude the project
steps.text:
Make a folder for the assistant, open Claude Code inside it, then give it the repo.

``` Command: Open Claude Code in a new folder
mkdir jarvis && cd jarvis
claude
```

Now paste this prompt into Claude Code (swap in your real link):

``` Prompt: Install the project
Clone this repo into the current folder, read its README, install all dependencies, and get it running. Tell me anything you need from me (API keys, config, etc.) as you go:
YOUR-REPO-URL
```

Claude pulls the files, sets up the dependencies, and starts the project on its own. When it needs something from you, like a key, it pauses and asks. Just answer in plain English.

> No project picked yet? Search GitHub for open-source "Claude voice assistant" or "voice MCP" projects and drop that link in. The setup flow works the same way.

steps.title: Add your ElevenLabs voice
steps.text:
This is what makes it talk.

Get your API key:

1. Sign in at elevenlabs.io.
2. Open your profile -> API Keys -> create a new key.
3. Copy it somewhere safe.

Pick a voice:

1. Go to the Voices or Voice Library section.
2. Preview a few and choose one you like.
3. Copy its Voice ID. You'll paste this into the config.

Plug it in. The easiest path is to let the official ElevenLabs MCP server handle speech. First install uv (a small helper), then add the server to Claude Code.

``` Command: Install uv and add ElevenLabs
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
claude mcp add elevenlabs --env ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=<your-key-here>
-- uvx elevenlabs-mcp
```

Or, if your project uses a .mcp.json file, add this block and paste your key inside:

``` Config: .mcp.json
{
"mcpServers": {
"elevenlabs": {
"command": "uvx",
"args": ["elevenlabs-mcp"],
"env": {
"ELEVENLABS_API_KEY": "<your-key-here>",
"ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID": "<your-voice-id>"
}
}
}
}
```

Then just tell Claude:

``` Prompt: Test the voice
Use ElevenLabs for the voice output, with the voice ID I set. Read this line out loud to test it: "Good morning, your assistant is online."
```

Restart Claude Code if it doesn't pick up the new server right away.

>! ElevenLabs voice generation uses credits. The free tier is plenty for testing. Heavy daily use may need a paid ElevenLabs plan.

steps.title: Connect your tools
steps.text:
Now link the assistant to the things you actually use: calendar, inbox, dashboards, notes, whatever. Each tool connects as an MCP server, exactly like ElevenLabs did. The pattern is always the same.

``` Command: Add a tool
claude mcp add <tool-name> --env KEY=value --
<command-to-run-that-server>
```

To see what's connected at any time:

``` Command: List connected tools
claude mcp list
```

Then let Claude wire the tool into your assistant's routine:

``` Prompt: Wire the tools in
I've connected my calendar and email. Update the assistant so my morning brief pulls from both: show me what's on my calendar today and which emails still need a reply.
```

> Most popular tools (Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion, Slack) have a ready-made MCP server. Search "[tool name] MCP server" for the exact install command, then add it with the same claude mcp add pattern. Start with one or two tools. You can always add more later.

steps.title: Run your first morning brief
steps.text:
Ask for it:

``` Prompt: Morning brief
Give me my morning brief out loud: what's pending, what's important, and which emails I still haven't replied to.
```

Instead of scrolling through 40 emails, you get a short spoken summary of what actually needs you. Once you like the format, ask Claude to save it as a reusable command or a scheduled routine so you can trigger it every morning with one word.

> If you're getting billed API rates while on Pro or Max, an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your environment is overriding your subscription. Run unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to use your plan instead.

> If an MCP server isn't showing up, restart Claude Code and run claude mcp list to confirm it's registered. If the install script returns a 403, it's usually a region, proxy or VPN issue. Try a different network, or use the npm install method.

``` Prompt: Install the YouTube Agent Skill
STEP 6: Show me a simple table of the 11 skills you installed, with one line on what each does.
```

steps.title: Restart and check

steps.title: Teach it your voice

Every skill reads one file: your voice file. Do this once and every script, title and reply sounds like you.

If you already have videos, paste this into Claude Code:

``` Prompt: Build my voice file from videos
Write my voice.md from these 3 videos and save it to
~/.claude/youtube/voice.md.

```

steps.title: Use the skills

Type the command, then your idea or file. Swap the examples for your own topics.

- /yt-script: turns one idea into a full script, with 5 scored hooks from 21 hook formulas. Try: /yt-script 5 free AI tools that replace a video editor
- /yt-package: writes 10 title options and a thumbnail idea for the best one. Try: /yt-package my video about free AI video editors
- /yt-edit: tells you where to cut (dead air, filler, retakes) with timecodes. Attach your transcript (.srt), then type /yt-edit
- /yt-comment: sorts your comments, drafts replies in your voice, and picks one to pin. Paste your comments, then type /yt-comment
- /yt-plan: plans your week around the hours you actually have. Try: /yt-plan I have 6 hours this week

- /yt-audit: reviews your whole channel and gives you ONE fix, not twenty. Try: /yt-audit my channel: [YOUR CHANNEL LINK]

To go from a viral idea straight to a finished package, paste this:

``` Prompt: Viral idea to script to package
Use /yt-viral on these channels: [3 to 5 channel links in your niche]. Pick the top idea I could make this week. Then use /yt-script to write it in my voice. Then use /yt-package to give me titles and a thumbnail idea.
```

> Thumbnails come out as a written brief (expression, framing, 3 words, background). You or your designer make the image. /yt-edit gives a cut list with timecodes, and you or your editor do the cutting.

> Hook scores are a guide, not a promise. A low score means look again, a high score is not a guarantee. If a skill needs a number it doesn't have, it asks you rather than making one up.
