title: Pit 100 Claudes against one prompt with Arena
summary: Arena is a free Claude skill that spins up 100 mini Claudes to answer the same prompt, critique each other, and eliminate the weak ones until only the best answer survives.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A laptop (Mac or Windows).
- A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Claude Code and Arena's agents run on your plan.
- 2 minutes for setup.

steps.title: Install Claude Code
steps.text:
This is the only manual install. After this, Claude handles everything for you.

On Mac, open Terminal and paste:

``` Command (Mac): Install Claude Code
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

On Windows, open PowerShell and paste:

``` Command (Windows): Install Claude Code
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

Once it finishes, type claude and press Enter. Log in with your Claude account when it asks.

> If claude is command not found, close and reopen the terminal, then try again.

steps.title: Install the Arena skill
steps.text:
Inside Claude Code, paste this message and drop the Arena repo link where shown:

``` Prompt: Install Arena
Install the Arena skill from this GitHub repo: [paste the repo link here]

Clone the repo, install it as a Claude skill, then run /skills to confirm it's loaded. Install any dependencies the repo needs.
```

Claude handles the clone, install and setup itself. When it's done, run /skills and you'll see Arena in the list.

> If the repo doesn't clone, paste: "Retry the Arena install and show me the exact error if it fails." If Arena doesn't show in /skills, paste: "Reload the skills directory and run /skills again."

steps.title: Run Arena on a prompt
steps.text:
In the same Claude Code window, paste:

``` Prompt: Run Arena
Use the Arena skill on this prompt:

[Paste the prompt you want 100 Claudes to fight over. Could be a coding problem, a piece of writing, a strategy question, a design decision, anything where you've already tried once and the answer wasn't sharp enough.]
```

steps.title: Watch the 100 Claudes fight
steps.text:
Here is what happens behind the scenes:

1. Arena spawns 100 mini Claudes, each getting the same prompt.
2. Each one solves it its own way, with different reasoning, structures and angles.
3. They review each other's answers and point out mistakes.
4. Weaker answers get eliminated round by round.
5. One winner survives, and that is what you see.

You watch the rounds happen in the terminal. The final answer comes with a short note on why it beat the others.

steps.title: When to reach for Arena
steps.text:
Arena uses far more plan credit than a normal Claude run, 100 agents instead of 1. Save it for prompts where:

- The first answer was clearly off.
- The task is open-ended and the best answer isn't obvious.
- You're about to ship, publish or send something and want the strongest version.
- You've re-prompted 2 to 3 times and keep getting similar, mediocre answers.

For simple questions, a normal Claude chat is fine. Arena is the heavy artillery.

>! Because Arena runs 100 agents at once, it uses a lot of your plan credit. If that feels like overkill, run it with fewer agents, for example: "Run Arena on this prompt with 20 agents instead of 100: [your prompt]".

> To use it again later, open Claude Code and paste: "Use the Arena skill on this: [your prompt]".

title: Scrape any site into a dashboard with Claude
summary: Connect Claude to Apify, paste a URL, and Claude picks the scraper, tests it, runs it, and turns the data into a searchable dashboard you can filter and export.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Connectors aren't on the free plan.
- An Apify account. The free plan includes $5 of usage credit a month.
- A website URL you want to scrape.
- About 10 minutes.

steps.title: Connect Claude to Apify
steps.text:
This is a one-time setup. After this, every future scrape is just one prompt.

1. Open Claude on desktop or web.
2. Go to Settings -> Connectors.
3. Search Apify and click **Connect**.
4. A browser tab opens. Sign in to Apify and click **Authorize**.
5. Come back to Claude. You'll see Apify listed as an active connector.

Claude can now run scrapers on your behalf.

steps.title: Paste the website and this prompt
steps.text:
Open a new chat in Claude and paste this, with your URL:

``` Prompt: Scrape a site
I want to scrape this website: [PASTE URL HERE]

Ask me what data I want to extract, then:
1. Pick the best Apify Actor for the job
2. Configure it for me
3. Run a small test first (5-10 items)
4. Show me a sample of what it pulled
5. If it looks right, run the full scrape
6. Save the results as a clean dataset

I want to see the data, not raw JSON.
```

Claude takes over from here.

steps.title: Answer Claude's questions
steps.text:
Claude asks 2 or 3 things. Answer in plain English, no config files and no code. For a Shopify store, for example, it might ask:

- Do you want product name, price, images, description, stock?
- How many products: all of them, or the top 100?
- Any specific category?

steps.title: Let it test first
steps.text:
Claude runs a small test scrape (5 to 10 items) before the full run. This saves your Apify credit if something is wrong. You'll see a small preview of the fields it pulled, like product name, price, image URL and stock.

If it looks right, tell Claude "run the full scrape." If a field is missing, tell Claude what to add, for example "also grab the review count."

steps.title: Get your dashboard
steps.text:
Once the full scrape is done, ask Claude:

``` Prompt: Build a dashboard
Build me a searchable dashboard for this data with:
- Search bar
- Filter by category and price
- Sort by any column
- Export to CSV
```

Claude builds it as an artifact. You can search any item instantly, filter by whatever fields you scraped, and download the whole thing as CSV or Excel.

steps.title: Turn it into a service (optional)
steps.text:
The same scrape-and-dashboard works as a paid service. Who pays for it:

- E-commerce brand: a competitor pricing dashboard, updated weekly.
- Real estate agent: every new listing in their city, filterable.
- Local business: a directory of every competitor and their offers.
- D2C founder: Amazon reviews of competitor products.
- Recruiter: every job posting from target companies.

A starting range is $200 to $500 for a one-time scrape plus dashboard, and $50 to $150 a month for weekly refreshes.

>! Don't scrape sites that block it. Check the site's robots.txt. Public product pages are usually fine, but sites like LinkedIn and Facebook are a hard no.

> Don't run huge scrapes on the free tier, the $5 credit runs out fast. Upgrade before a paid client project.

> Always test one page first, even on a site you've scraped before, because pages change. And save the exact prompt you used, since the same prompt on the same site gives you a repeatable delivery.

title: Turn Claude Code into a senior UI engineer
summary: Three free Claude skills plus two MCP servers give Claude Code real design taste and let it design in Figma, build the site, and test it in a real browser. Installs in about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- Claude Code installed and authenticated.
- Node.js 18 or newer on your PATH.
- The Figma desktop app (the web version won't work for the Figma MCP) and a Figma Dev or Full seat.
- Any project folder to test the stack in.

The stack is five pieces: three skills (Emil Kowalski, Impeccable, Taste) are the design brain, and two MCP servers (Figma, Playwright) are the hands and eyes.

steps.title: Install the Emil Kowalski skill
steps.text:
This one handles animation craft, easing and the small details that make interfaces feel right. In your terminal, run:

``` Command: Install the Emil skill
npx skills add emilkowalski/skills --agent claude-code
```

It installs 6 sub-skills into .claude/skills/ of the current project:

- emil-design-eng: the main skill (UI polish, animation decisions, component design).
- review-animations: audits your animations against Emil's rules.
- improve-animations: returns prioritized fix plans.
- find-animation-opportunities: surfaces where motion helps, and where it hurts.
- prototype: builds several genuinely different versions of a UI piece.
- One more focused on design-decision reviews. They trigger automatically when you ask Claude to build, review or improve UI. To check, ask Claude "What skills do you have available?" and you should see the six Emil skills.

steps.title: Install the Impeccable skill
steps.text:
Impeccable adds about 20 slash commands for typography, color contrast, spacing and interaction states. Inside Claude Code, run these two commands:

``` Command: Install Impeccable
/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable
/plugin install impeccable@impeccable
```

The one you'll use constantly is /polish. It runs a full cleanup pass on the current file: typography, color contrast, spacing, interaction states, focus rings, dialog behaviour. It's the fastest way to make an AI-generated page not look AI-generated.

steps.title: Install the Taste skill
steps.text:
The Taste skill blocks generic AI output and pulls from a curated library of well-designed sites. Pick one option.

Option A, the standalone community version (sharpest anti-slop discipline, most adopted):

``` Command: Install Taste (Option A)
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

Option B, a merged version that combines Emil, Impeccable and Taste into one deduplicated skill. Worth it if you find the three separate skills overlap:

``` Command: Install Taste (Option B)
npx skills add h3nryprod01/design-taste
```

steps.title: Set up the Figma MCP server
steps.text:
Use the official plugin path. In your terminal, run:

``` Command: Install the Figma plugin
claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official
```

Then restart Claude Code, run /plugin, open the **Installed** tab, select figma, press Enter, and complete the OAuth flow when the browser opens.

Next, turn on Figma's Dev Mode MCP server on the Figma side:

1. Open the Figma Desktop app (not the web version).
2. Open a Figma Design file.
3. With nothing selected, switch to **Dev Mode**.
4. In the right sidebar, enable the **MCP Server**.
5. You'll see confirmation the server is running.

Test it by selecting a frame in Figma and prompting:

``` Prompt: Convert a Figma frame
Convert my current Figma selection into a React component with TailwindCSS.
```

steps.title: Install the Playwright MCP server
Use the full stack
steps.text:
Once everything is installed, the whole loop runs in one prompt. For example:

``` Prompt: Build a landing page
Build a landing page for a fintech SaaS called "Vault" - modern, minimal, with a strong hero, three feature cards, pricing (3 tiers), and a footer. Use Next.js + Tailwind + shadcn/ui.
```

Under the hood: Taste reads the brief and pulls real reference direction, Emil decides what deserves motion and which easing to use, Impeccable enforces typography, contrast, spacing and states, Claude builds the code with all three as constraints, and Playwright opens the page in a real browser, checks mobile, tablet and desktop, and flags anything broken. Claude iterates until Playwright confirms it works.

If you have a Figma design ready, this does it in one shot:

``` Prompt: Figma to production code
Convert the design in my currently-selected Figma frame into production code. Match it pixel-perfectly. Test it in the browser when done.
```

title: Run your resume past a 7-Claude hiring panel
summary: Paste your resume and a target job description, and a 7-reviewer panel inside Claude, from the ATS to a skeptic, judges you independently, then rewrites your resume with every weakness fixed.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- Your current resume (copy the text, or have the file ready to upload).
- The full job description for the role you actually want.
- A Claude chat open at claude.ai.

> Always give the panel a real job description. A resume isn't good or bad in a vacuum, it's good for a specific role, and the panel gets far sharper when it has a target to judge you against.

steps.title: Open a fresh Claude chat
steps.text: Start a new conversation so nothing earlier pollutes the review.

steps.title: Paste the panel prompt and fill in the blanks
steps.text:
Copy the prompt below into Claude, but don't send it yet. First replace [PASTE THE JOB DESCRIPTION HERE] and [PASTE YOUR RESUME HERE] with your real text, then send. The panel is seven independent reviewers: the ATS, the recruiter, the hiring manager, a rival applicant, the CEO, a future teammate, and a skeptic. Each one judges you alone and doesn't see the others until the final summary.

``` Prompt: The 7-person hiring panel
You are going to run my resume through a 7-person hiring panel for a specific job.

RULES:
- Each reviewer works INDEPENDENTLY and does not see the other reviewers' verdicts.
- Each reviewer judges my resume ONLY against the job description below.
- Be blunt and specific. I want the truth, not encouragement.
- No generic advice - every point must reference something actually in my resume.

For EACH of the 7 reviewers, give me exactly this:
- VERDICT: PASS / BORDERLINE / REJECT
- SCORE: x/10
- TOP 3 reasons for the verdict (specific to my resume)
- THE ONE THING to fix that would most change their mind

Here are the 7 reviewers and what each cares about:
1. THE ATS - automated screener. Does it pass keyword match, required qualifications, and clean formatting to reach a human at all?
2. THE RECRUITER - an 8-second human skim. Fit, gaps, red flags, level signals.
3. THE HIRING MANAGER - interview yes/no. Impact, relevance to THIS role, proof over claims.
4. A RIVAL APPLICANT - reads competitively. Where would a similar candidate beat me?
5. THE CEO / EXECUTIVE - the business case. ROI, outcomes, ownership, leadership.
6. A FUTURE TEAMMATE - "do I want to work with this person?" Clarity, collaboration, culture, trust.
7. THE SKEPTIC - devil's advocate. Vague claims, buzzwords, unverifiable numbers, filler.

AFTER all 7 reviews, give me:
A) PANEL SUMMARY - the overall verdict, my average score, and the 3 problems that showed up across the most reviewers. B) THE REWRITE - a full, improved version of my resume with every issue fixed:
stronger bullet points, real metrics where I have them (ask me
if you need
numbers), tightened language, and ATS-friendly formatting. Keep
it truthful -
never invent experience, titles, or results I didn't give you.

=== JOB DESCRIPTION ===
[PASTE THE JOB DESCRIPTION HERE]

=== MY RESUME ===
[PASTE YOUR RESUME HERE]
```

steps.title: Read your panel report
steps.text:
Claude returns a verdict, a score, and the single biggest fix from each of the 7 reviewers, then a combined summary.

> Fix the cross-reviewer problems first. If 5 of 7 reviewers flag the same weakness, that's your highest-leverage edit.

steps.title: Get your rewritten resume
steps.text:
The prompt ends by asking Claude for a fixed, bulletproof version of your resume with every issue addressed.

> Be honest with Claude. The rewrite is only as truthful as what you give it, so never let it invent titles or results. And keep real numbers: "Grew revenue 40%" beats "responsible for growth" with every reviewer.

steps.title: Push it further (optional)
steps.text:
Use these one at a time, after the first report.

To go deeper on one reviewer:

``` Prompt: Go deeper on one reviewer
Reviewer 3 (the Hiring Manager) rejected me. Walk me through my resume line by line as that person, and show me how to rewrite each weak bullet.
```

To add your real metrics:

``` Prompt: Add real metrics
Here are the real numbers from my last job: [paste details]. Rework my bullet points to use these, and flag any claim that still sounds vague.
```

To tailor the same resume to a different job:

``` Prompt: Tailor to a second job
Here's a different job description: [paste it]. Re-run only the ATS and Hiring Manager, and tell me what to change so the SAME resume fits this role.
```

For a final polish:

``` Prompt: Final polish
Give me the final resume as clean, copy-paste-ready text with consistent formatting, strong action verbs, and no buzzwords. Then list 5 things I should still double-check myself.
```

> Run the panel per job, not once. The same resume scores differently against different roles, so re-run it for each serious application.

title: Turn messy ideas into pro prompts with Prompt Master
summary: Prompt Master is a free Claude skill that turns a messy one-liner into a production-grade prompt for any AI tool, auto-detecting the target and catching the patterns that waste tokens.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A Claude.ai account, or Claude Code installed.
- About 60 seconds. No Python, no Node, no API keys.

steps.title: Install Prompt Master
steps.text:
Pick the path for where you want it to live.

Path A, into claude.ai (the simplest):

1. Go to the repo (link in Tools).
2. Click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**.
3. Open claude.ai.
4. In the sidebar, go to **Customize** -> **Skills**.
5. Click **Upload** and drop in the ZIP.
6. Done. Prompt Master is now available in every chat.

Path B, into Claude Code (for developers). Clone it into your global skills folder:

``` Command: Install into Claude Code (global)
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/nidhinjs/prompt-master.git ~/.claude/skills/prompt-master
```

Restart Claude Code and it's available in every project. For one project only, clone it into that repo instead:

``` Command: Install into one project
git clone https://github.com/nidhinjs/prompt-master.git .claude/skills/prompt-master
```

Path C, into Cursor. Same pattern, different folder:

``` Command: Install into Cursor
git clone https://github.com/nidhinjs/prompt-master.git ~/.cursor/skills/prompt-master
```

>! Do NOT place it in ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/. That folder is reserved for Cursor's built-in skills, and putting third-party ones there breaks things.

steps.title: Invoke it
steps.text:
Four ways to call it. All use the same engine, but each enters a different mode.

Style 1, natural language (most common). Just describe what you want:

``` Prompt: Natural language
Turn this into a proper prompt: I want Claude to build a landing page for my dog grooming business
```

Prompt Master detects the target, picks the right architecture, catches the missing details (no colours, no sections, no stack), and returns a finished prompt.

Style 2, explicit invocation, for tighter control when the target isn't obvious:

``` Prompt: Explicit invocation
/prompt-master
Target: Midjourney
Task: A cinematic hero shot of my product
```

Style 3, decompiler mode, to reverse-engineer an existing prompt:

``` Prompt: Decompile a prompt
Decompile this prompt and tell me what's wrong with it:

"Write me a blog post about AI. Make it engaging."
```

It identifies which patterns the prompt violates and returns a rewritten version with the fixes annotated.

Style 4, cross-tool translation, to move a prompt from one tool's dialect to another:

``` Prompt: Translate across tools
Take this Midjourney prompt and translate it to Sora:

"cinematic wide shot, golden hour, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field"
```

> As an example of what you get, typing "help me build the landing page for my SaaS, it's like Linear but for lawyers" comes back as a full prompt with the context, objective, style, tone, audience, stack, section order, file structure and stop-conditions all filled in, so the AI never has to ask a clarifying question.

title: Build a live data dashboard from a folder in Claude
summary: Point Claude at a folder of CSVs or a connected app and it builds an interactive dashboard that re-pulls your data, picks the charts, and can answer plain-English questions about the numbers.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Pro is $20 a month ($17 a month billed annually). This isn't on the free plan.
- Claude on web, desktop, or mobile. Reading a local folder needs the desktop app, but a connected data source (Google Drive, Notion, and so on) works anywhere.
- A data source, one of: a local folder of CSV, XLSX or JSON files, or a connected app (Google Drive, Notion, Airtable, Slack, or a custom MCP server).

> Cowork and chat are now one Claude, so you don't install anything separate. The dashboard is an artifact Claude builds for you.

steps.title: Prepare your data
steps.text:
Pick whichever you have.

For a local folder: make a folder anywhere on your computer and drop your files in, for example a folder called company-data holding sales-2026-q3.csv, customer-list.csv and product-inventory.xlsx. Claude can read CSV, XLSX, JSON, plain text and markdown.

For a connected app (best for a dashboard that stays live for a team):

1. In Claude, open the sidebar and go to **Connectors**.
2. Enable the connector for your data source (Google Drive, Notion, and so on).
3. Complete the sign-in. Claude can now pull from that source, so the dashboard reflects the source whenever it updates.

steps.title: Ask Claude to build the dashboard
steps.text:
Start a new chat and paste this, pointing it at your folder:

``` Prompt: Build the dashboard
Build me an interactive dashboard artifact from the folder at ~/Desktop/company-data.

Requirements:
- Read all the CSV and XLSX files in the folder
- Pick the most useful chart types based on the columns
- Include a "Refresh" button that re-reads the data each click and updates every chart
- Add a natural-language chat box at the bottom that can answer questions about the data, like "what's our best-performing region this quarter?"
- Show the timestamp of when the data was last refreshed
- Design: clean, professional, minimal, with colours that work on both light and dark backgrounds
- Layout: KPI cards at the top, charts in the middle, chat box at the bottom, and the raw-data table collapsed by default
```

If your data is in a connected app instead, change the first line to name it, for example: "Build me an interactive dashboard artifact from my Google Drive folder called Company Data using the Google Drive connector." Keep the rest the same.

Claude reads your data (or calls the connector), picks the visualizations, and drops the dashboard into your Artifacts view.

steps.title: Open it and refresh
steps.text: Open the artifact from your Artifacts view. It opens in its own persistent view, and re-reads the folder or re-calls the connector so you see current data. The chat box lives inside the dashboard, and because it runs as whoever is using it, each person needs their own Claude access to ask it questions.

steps.title: Share it (Team or Enterprise)
steps.text: On a Team or Enterprise plan you can share the artifact inside your organization. Whoever opens it signs in with the same organization, and it connects to their own connectors and data. There are no public or external links yet. On Pro the dashboard stays private to your account.

title: Run your decision past a 5-advisor LLM Council
summary: LLM Council is a free Claude Code skill that runs your question past five independent advisors, from a contrarian to an executor, makes them peer-review each other, and ends with one chairman's verdict.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Claude Code isn't on the free plan.
- Claude Code installed and authenticated, or Claude on claude.ai.
- Nothing else. No API keys, no MCP servers, no scripts. It's a pure skill that runs on subagents.

steps.title: Install LLM Council
steps.text:
Pick a path. Path A is the easiest.

Path A, let Claude install it for you. Open Claude Code (or claude.ai) and paste this:

``` Prompt: Install LLM Council
Please install this Claude skill for me. The SKILL.md file lives at:

https://github.com/oliwoodman/llm-council-skill

Set it up as a global skill so I can use it in any project.
Walk me through anything you need from me.
```

Claude fetches the file, creates the folder at ~/.claude/skills/llm-council/, and confirms it's ready. Restart Claude Code once and you're done.

Path B, clone it into your global skills folder yourself:

``` Command: Install by git clone
git clone https://github.com/oliwoodman/llm-council-skill ~/.claude/skills/llm-council
```

Path C, a single command, no git needed (this uses a fork with the same advisor structure):

``` Command: Install by skill add
claude skill add --url
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automatorsplus/llm-council-skill/main/.claude/skills/llm-council/SKILL.md
```

steps.title: Run a council
steps.text:
Open any Claude Code session and start your message with the trigger phrase, then your question:

``` Prompt: Run a council
council this: [your question or decision]
```

For example:

- council this: should I quit my job to build my SaaS full-time?
- council this: my agency is doing $10k a month, should I hire my first employee or stay solo?
- council this: I'm considering raising my consulting rate from $50 to $100 an hour. Do I lose more clients than I gain?
- pressure-test this: I want to launch a paid community at $29 a month for founders. Here's my plan: [describe it]

Claude spins up the 5 advisors in parallel, runs an anonymous peer review, then the chairman's verdict. A full council takes about 4 to 6 minutes.

steps.title: Read the verdict
steps.text:
Five advisors each answer first, each from one lens:

- The Contrarian: hunts for the fatal flaw, what's missing, what will fail. Won't hedge.
- The First Principles Thinker: asks if you're even solving the right problem, and reframes it from the ground up.
- The Expansionist: looks for the upside everyone else missed, ignoring risk (that's the Contrarian's job).
- The Outsider: has zero context about you or your field, and reacts purely to what's in front of it.
- The Executor: only cares what you actually do first. Every answer maps to "what do you do Monday morning?".

Then all five peer-review each other anonymously, grading the others without knowing who wrote what, which keeps the review honest instead of defensive. Finally the Chairman commits to one verdict under about 250 words: the call (go, don't, or conditional), the strongest reason, the biggest risk, and the next step within 7 days. If Claude starts to hedge, the skill forces it to commit.

> The Outsider is the most underrated advisor. Run "council this: [your product description]" and it tells you what a first-time visitor doesn't understand about your product, the way a stranger would read your landing page. That's often worth more than the other four combined.

> This skill runs 5 subagents that are all Claude, different lenses on one model. If you want the real multi-model version, where Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok argue and peer-review each other, that's Andrej Karpathy's original (link in Links). It's a local web app, about 15 minutes to set up, and needs an OpenRouter API key with roughly $5 to $10 in credits.

title: Make any photo move like you with Wan AI
summary: Wan AI's Animate tool copies your expressions and movements from a video you record onto any character in a photo, and renders it as an HD video, free in the browser.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- A wan.video account. Sign in with Google or email, no app or download.
- A clear, front-facing reference photo of the character you want to animate.
- A short video of yourself, 5 to 15 seconds, doing the motion you want.
- A browser. Free credits are added to your account on signup, enough to test it a few times.

>! Only animate photos you have the right to use, and don't use this to impersonate a real person. Putting someone's face on your movements without their consent can cause real harm.

steps.title: Sign in at wan.video
steps.text:
1. Open wan.video in your browser.
2. Click **Sign in** (top right).
3. Sign in with Google, or use email.

steps.title: Open the Wan Animate tool
steps.text:
1. On the homepage, click **Create** (or **Generate**) in the top menu.
2. In the sidebar, find **Video -> Wan Animate** (sometimes shown as **Animate** or **Move**).
3. Click it to open the animation workspace. You'll see two upload slots, one for the image and one for the video.

steps.title: Upload your reference image
steps.text:
This is the character that will move. Best results come from a clear, front-facing photo with the full face visible, no heavy shadows, head-and-shoulders or half-body, and only one subject in the frame.

Avoid side profiles, faces covered by hands, sunglasses or masks, photos with more than one person, and anything low-resolution or blurry.

Click the **Image** slot, drag your photo in (or click to browse), and wait for the preview to load.

steps.title: Record and upload your driving video
steps.text:
This is the video Wan copies the motion from. Frame yourself from the chest or waist up (the more of you is visible, the more movement it can transfer), face the camera directly, with even lighting and a plain background. Keep it to 5 to 15 seconds, and do whatever you want the character to do: talk, laugh, wave, gesture.

Shoot it on your phone and upload the file, or record directly in Wan if that option is there. Then click the **Video** slot, upload the clip, and wait a few seconds for it to process.

steps.title: Set your output and generate
steps.text:
Check the side panel before you generate:

- Resolution: 720p or 1080p. 1080p costs more credits but is worth it for social.
- Aspect ratio: 9:16 for Reels and Shorts, 16:9 for YouTube, 1:1 for square.
- Duration: matches your driving video by default.
- Mode or style: pick "Animate" or "Motion Transfer", not "Replace" or "Relight" unless that's what you want.

Then click **Generate**. The video queues and renders, usually 1 to 3 minutes for a short clip. Leave the tab open and watch the progress bar.

steps.title: Review and download
steps.text:
When it finishes, the preview auto-plays. Watch it end to end and check three things: the character still looks like the reference, the movements match your video, and there's no weird warping around hands or edges. If it looks good, click **Download** and save the MP4. If it looks off, tweak the reference image or driving video (better lighting, cleaner background, simpler motion) and run it again.

> The first shot rarely lands perfect, so budget 2 to 3 generations for one clean output. Simpler driving motion gives a cleaner result, and keeping your hands away from your face avoids the most common finger and hand glitches. Match the character's proportions to yours, since a very different head-to-body ratio can cause stretching.

> Once you have a clean output, record your motion once and apply it to several reference images to keep one character consistent across a whole series.

title: Keep Claude Code running past its limits with 9Router
summary: 9Router is a free local proxy that sits between your coding tool and 40+ AI providers. When your Claude plan hits its limit, it switches to a cheap or free backup mid-session so you keep working.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- Node.js 18 or newer, and npm.
- Claude Code, or any coding tool with a custom endpoint field.
- A browser for the dashboard.
- Best paired with an existing Claude plan (Max especially). 9Router shines as the fallback when you already have one.

steps.title: Install and start 9Router
steps.text:
Open your terminal and install it:

``` Command: Install 9Router
npm install -g 9router
```

Then start it:

``` Command: Start 9Router
9router
```

It prints a dashboard address and an API endpoint, both on port 20128.

If you'd rather have a guided 5-minute onboarding that walks you through provider setup, use the starter kit instead:

``` Command: Starter kit (optional)
git clone https://github.com/aiflowlearn/9router-starter-kit
cd 9router-starter-kit
./install.sh
./configure.sh
```

steps.title: Open the dashboard
steps.text: Go to http://localhost:20128 in your browser. You'll land on the Providers page with nothing connected yet.

steps.title: Connect providers (start with 2 or 3)
steps.text:
Click **Providers** and pick from the list. A good beginner stack across three tiers:

- Tier 1, your subscription: Claude Code. Click **Connect** and sign in. 9Router now tracks your 5-hour and weekly quotas in real time.
- Tier 2, cheap paid backups: GLM (Z.ai) at about $0.60 per 1M tokens (sign up at z.ai, create an API key, paste it), and MiniMax at about $0.20 per 1M (sign up at minimax.io, create a key, paste it).
- Tier 3, free fallbacks: iFlow (free Kimi K2 Thinking, OAuth login), Qwen (free Qwen models, OAuth login), and Kiro (free Claude 4.5, GLM-5 and MiniMax, via AWS Builder ID, Google or GitHub login).

Every free connection is one browser click, no credit card. Provider prices are set by the providers and can change, so check their sites.

>! Don't add Gemini CLI to this chain if you plan to use it from non-Gemini tools. Google's terms restrict free Gemini CLI tokens to Gemini CLI itself, and routing them through 9Router in Claude Code may get your account banned. The dashboard flags this next to Gemini CLI, so respect that flag.

steps.title: Build your fallback chain
steps.text:
In the dashboard, go to **Combos** and click **Create Combo**. A solid chain for a Claude Code user, in order:

1. Your Claude Code subscription (use it fully first).
2. A cheap backup for when the quota runs out, such as GLM 5.2.
3. A free emergency fallback, such as Kimi K2 Thinking via iFlow.

Save the combo. The result: your existing Claude plan does the heavy lifting, a few dollars of cheap overflow covers the gaps, and the free tier catches the rest, so your plan's limits stop interrupting you mid-task.

steps.title: Point Claude Code at 9Router
steps.text:
Generate a dashboard key in the 9Router dashboard under **Settings** -> **API Keys**, then in your terminal:

``` Command: Route Claude Code through 9Router
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="your-9router-dashboard-key"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-with-fallback"
claude
```

Use your own combo's name in place of claude-with-fallback. That's the whole setup.

steps.title: Turn on RTK Token Saver
steps.text:
In the dashboard, go to **Settings** -> **RTK Token Saver** -> **Enable**. RTK compresses tool_result outputs (long file dumps, terminal logs, JSON blobs) before they reach the model, for about 20 to 40% token savings depending on how tool-heavy your work is. Your source code is preserved exactly; RTK only compresses the noise around it.

> For heavier compression, also enable Caveman mode alongside RTK. Combined savings can reach around 65% on log-heavy sessions.

steps.title: Check the fallback works
steps.text:
1. Use Claude Code normally until you approach your 5-hour limit (the dashboard shows a countdown).
2. Watch the "current provider" indicator in the dashboard.
3. When the Claude quota runs out, the indicator flips to your Tier 2 provider (for example GLM 5.2).
4. Keep coding. Same interface, different backend, no re-auth.

steps.title: Point other tools at 9Router (optional)
steps.text:
Same base URL, different settings per tool. In Cursor, set a custom endpoint to http://localhost:20128/v1 with your dashboard key. For Cline, Continue, RooCode or any OpenAI-compatible tool, set the base URL to http://localhost:20128/v1 in its config. For the Codex CLI:

``` Command: Route Codex through 9Router
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-9router-dashboard-key"
```

title: Run a free image, video and lip-sync AI studio
summary: Open Generative AI is one open-source app that bundles image, video and lip-sync generation across 200+ models into a single studio you can self-host or run in the browser.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- Node.js 18 or newer and npm (for the self-host route).
- A Muapi.ai account for the API key. The app is free, but generation runs through Muapi and is pay-per-use.
- macOS, Windows, or Linux.

>! You only generate with photos, voices and footage you have the right to use. Lip-sync turns a photo plus any voice into a talking video, so don't use it to impersonate a real person.

steps.title: Install it
steps.text:
Three paths. A and B are fastest to try; C is the full self-host.

Path A, hosted web version (no install): open muapi.ai/open-generative-ai, click **Settings**, paste your Muapi API key (Step 2), and start generating.

Path B, desktop app: on the repo's **Releases** page, download the .dmg (macOS), .exe (Windows) or .AppImage (Linux), install it, and paste your Muapi key on first launch.

Path C, self-host. Clone the repo:

``` Command: Clone the repo
git clone --recurse-submodules
https://github.com/Anil-matcha/Open-Generative-AI.git
cd Open-Generative-AI
```

Set it up (plain npm install isn't enough; this builds the workspace packages first):

``` Command: Set up
npm run setup
```

Launch it, then open http://localhost:3000 in your browser:

``` Command: Launch
npm run dev
```

> The desktop app is unsigned, so macOS shows "cannot verify developer" (right-click, then Open) and Windows SmartScreen may block it (click More info, then Run anyway). Both are normal for small open-source projects.

steps.title: Get and paste your Muapi key
steps.text:
1. Go to muapi.ai and sign up.
2. New signups usually get some free trial credits, but the amount varies, so confirm your current balance before you generate.
3. Open **API Keys**, click **Create Key**, and copy it.
4. On first launch the app asks for the key. Paste it. It's stored locally in your browser's localStorage and only ever sent to Muapi.

steps.title: What's in the four studios
steps.text:
- Image Studio: text-to-image and image-to-image across 50+ models (Flux, Midjourney, Ideogram, SDXL, Nano Banana 2, GPT-4o), plus multi-image input (up to 14 references) on compatible models.
- Video Studio: text-to-video and image-to-video across many models (Sora 2, Veo 3, Kling v3, Wan 2.6, Seedance 2.0 and Pro, Hailuo 2.3, Runway Gen-3). Aspect ratios 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, durations typically 5, 10 or 15 seconds.
- Lip Sync Studio: portrait image plus audio into a talking video, or an existing video plus audio into a lip-synced video. Nine models across the two modes.
- Cinema Studio: a style layer with preset camera, lens, focal length and aperture controls, for when prompt words alone aren't giving you the look.

steps.title: Make a talking video from a photo
steps.text:
1. Open Lip Sync Studio and switch to portrait plus audio mode.
2. Upload your photo.
3. Upload or record an audio clip in the voice you want (or generate one with a TTS tool).
4. Pick a model: Infinite Talk I2V for realism, LatentSync for speed.
5. Set the aspect ratio and duration.
6. Generate.

steps.title: Make a cinematic video from a photo
steps.text:
1. Open Video Studio and switch to image-to-video mode.
2. Upload your photo.
3. Paste a prompt like the one below.

``` Prompt: Cinematic motion
Cinematic slow push-in, warm sunset lighting, film grain, shallow depth of field.
```

4. Pick a high-quality model such as Seedance 2.0 Pro or Kling v3.
5. Set the aspect to 16:9 and the duration to 5 to 10 seconds.
6. Generate.

title: Run your coding tool on free and cheap AI with OmniRoute
summary: OmniRoute is a free local proxy that connects your coding tool to 200+ AI providers, routes each prompt to the cheapest option, falls back when one runs out, and compresses prompts to save tokens.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- Node.js 18 or newer and npm (or Docker instead).
- A coding tool with a custom endpoint: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Cline, Copilot, Windsurf, Continue, or any OpenAI-compatible tool.
- A browser for the dashboard.

steps.title: Install OmniRoute
steps.text:
Pick one. npm is the simplest.

``` Command: Install with npm
npm install -g omniroute
```

Or run it with Docker:

``` Command: Run with Docker
docker run -p 20128:20128 diegosouzapw/omniroute
```

Or download the desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux) from omniroute.online. To check the npm install worked:

``` Command: Check the version
omniroute --version
```

steps.title: Launch it
steps.text:
Start OmniRoute:

``` Command: Launch OmniRoute
omniroute
```

It prints a dashboard address and an API endpoint, both on port 20128.

steps.title: Connect a few free providers
steps.text:
Open http://localhost:20128/dashboard, go to **Providers**, and connect a few free tiers. Strong ones to start with:

- iFlow (Kimi K2 Thinking): free, sign in with OAuth.
- Qwen: free models, OAuth.
- Kiro: free Claude 4.5, GLM-5 and MiniMax, via AWS Builder ID, Google or GitHub.
- NVIDIA NIM: free credits included, sign up.
- Groq: fast free tier, API key.
- DeepSeek: free tokens on signup, API key.
- GitHub Copilot: free tier, GitHub OAuth.

Click **Connect** on any of these, no credit card needed. You can connect several and OmniRoute will use them all.

>! Don't route Gemini CLI's free tokens through OmniRoute into other tools. Google's terms restrict free Gemini CLI tokens to Gemini CLI itself, and using them elsewhere can get your account banned. Connect it only if you'll use it from Gemini CLI.

steps.title: Point your coding tool at OmniRoute
steps.text:
Generate a dashboard key at **Dashboard** -> **Settings** -> **API Keys**, then point your tool's base URL at OmniRoute: http://localhost:20128/v1

For Claude Code, in your terminal:

``` Command: Route Claude Code
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="your-dashboard-key"
claude
```

For Cursor, Windsurf or Antigravity, set a custom endpoint to http://localhost:20128/v1 in Settings. For the Codex CLI:

``` Command: Route Codex
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-dashboard-key"
```

For any other OpenAI-compatible tool, replace its openai.com base URL with http://localhost:20128/v1 and use your dashboard key.

steps.title: Set your routing combo
steps.text:
In the dashboard, go to **Combos** and build a chain. OmniRoute uses it in order and falls back down the list when one runs out. Three starters:

- free-only: a chain of free providers such as Gemini 3 Flash, Kimi K2 Thinking and Qwen3 Coder Plus. Cost stays at $0 as long as you only use free tiers.
- maximize-Claude: your Claude Code subscription first, a cheap backup like GLM 4.7 second, and a free fallback like Kimi K2 Thinking third.
- always-on: a longer chain (Claude, a GPT codex model, GLM, MiniMax, then a free model) so a run rarely stops on you.

Save a combo and use its alias (for example omniroute/free-only) as the model name in your coding tool.

> Free tiers are set by the providers and can change or disappear, so treat a $0 setup as nice-to-have, not guaranteed.

steps.title: Turn on compression
steps.text:
In the dashboard, go to **Settings** -> **Compression** and pick a mode. It trades a little quality for fewer tokens:

- Off: for debugging OmniRoute itself.
- Lite: about 15% savings, safest.
- Standard: about 30%, a good default.
- Aggressive: about 50%, for long coding sessions.
- Ultra: about 75%, the most savings with some quality tradeoff.

title: Turn one keyword into a finished short video
summary: MoneyPrinterTurbo is a free open-source pipeline that takes one keyword and builds a finished short video, script, voiceover, subtitles, music and stock footage, through a simple web UI.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text:
- Docker Desktop and Git installed. On Windows, set up WSL2 first.
- A free Pexels API key (from pexels.com/api) for the stock footage.
- An LLM provider and its API key, for the script. Free lanes exist (Ollama running locally, g4f, Pollinations, ModelScope); paid lanes (DeepSeek, OpenAI) cost about a cent per video.
- 8 GB of RAM realistically. 4 GB only works in the all-cloud setup, and a local Ollama model needs 8 to 16 GB.
- About 5 GB free disk, and 15 to 30 minutes for the first setup (the Docker image is about 3 GB).

>! This is two keys, not one, a Pexels key and an LLM key. And "setup in 10 seconds" is only the command time. The first real install is 15 to 30 minutes, mostly the Docker download.

steps.title: Get your API keys
steps.text:
Stock footage (free): sign up at pexels.com and copy the API key from your account.

LLM provider, pick one lane:

- Free and cloud: g4f, Pollinations or ModelScope. Costs $0, but quality varies and it can be flaky.
- Free and local: Ollama. Costs $0 but needs 8 to 16 GB of RAM for the model, installed separately.
- Paid and reliable: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot or AIHubMix. Best script quality, roughly $0.001 per 60-second video.

For your first run, DeepSeek is the best price-to-quality balance (a few cents runs dozens of videos). For a strictly free path, Pollinations or g4f with Pexels footage gets you to a finished video at $0.

steps.title: Clone and configure
steps.text:
In your terminal:

``` Command: Clone and copy the config
git clone https://github.com/harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo.git
cd MoneyPrinterTurbo
cp config.example.toml config.toml
```

On Windows, use copy instead of cp. Then open config.toml and fill in the three things that matter, matching the provider block to your choice:

``` Config: config.toml
# 1. Stock footage
pexels_api_keys = ["YOUR_PEXELS_KEY_HERE"]

# 2. Which LLM to use
llm_provider = "deepseek" # or: openai, moonshot, ollama, g4f, pollinations, etc.

# 3. That provider's key and base URL (block name matches llm_provider) [deepseek] api_key = "YOUR_LLM_KEY_HERE" base_url = "https://api.deepseek.com"model_name = "deepseek-chat"
```

Each provider has its own block in config.toml with the keys it needs, and the file is well-commented, so just fill in the block that matches your llm_provider.

> For the free local lane, set llm_provider = "ollama", then in the [ollama] block set base_url to http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1 and model_name to whatever you've pulled (for example llama3.1:8b). Run ollama list to confirm.

steps.title: Launch
steps.text:
Use the prebuilt image (faster):

``` Command: Launch (prebuilt image)
docker compose -f docker-compose.release.yml up
```

Or build it locally (slower, only needed if you've changed the code):

``` Command: Launch (build locally)
docker compose up
```

The first run pulls about 3 GB of layers, so give it 10 to 20 minutes. Two services come up: the web UI at http://localhost:8501 and the REST API with docs at http://localhost:8080/docs.

> To manage it, run docker compose ps to see both containers, docker compose logs -f webui to watch the logs, and docker compose down to stop and clean up.

steps.title: Make your first video
steps.text:
Open http://localhost:8501 in your browser. In the Streamlit UI:

1. Topic: type one keyword or short phrase, such as "health", "morning routines" or "space facts".
2. Language and aspect ratio: pick English and 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and TikTok.
3. Voice: start with en-US-AndrewNeural or any Edge TTS voice. They're free and sound natural.
4. Subtitles: leave "edge" selected (fast, no GPU). Switch to "whisper" later if accuracy matters more than speed.
5. Click Generate. The UI streams each stage: script, search terms, footage download, voiceover, subtitles, then the FFmpeg encode.

The output lands in storage/tasks/<task_id>/final-1.mp4.

> If you see Chinese voices by default, the project is from a Chinese maintainer, so just pick an en-US voice in the dropdown. If it generates nothing or empty footage, it's almost always the Pexels key (check storage/logs/), or your topic is too abstract, so try a more concrete keyword.

steps.title: Use the REST API (optional)
steps.text:
To wire this into a pipeline instead of clicking the UI, the API docs are auto-generated at http://localhost:8080/docs. Every UI capability is a REST endpoint: submit a task, poll for the task_id, and download the MP4 when it's ready. Good for batch jobs or scheduled runs.

>! The output is a draft, not publish-ready. Stock-footage relevance varies a lot, and abstract themes often pull odd clips, so always preview before posting. Pexels and Pixabay are royalty-free for most uses, but check each clip's license if you publish commercially or at scale (the task logs list the source URLs).
